Calculate the pixel's position $\mathbf{p}$ in the same coordinate system as the element [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the pixelization routine transforms mesh values into an image buffer. It details the process where, for each pixel in the image plane, the sign of the dot product between the pixel's position and face normal vectors is calculated to determine containment. This calculation inherently requires and uses the pixel's position within the same coordinate system as the element (defined by its centroid and face normals) to perform the containment test and subsequent value deposition.

The claim states that vertex ordering (CW/CCW) is not required for the containment test because it relies on dot product signs relative to the centroid. Both the 'Source [S1] notes' and the 'Source [S1] passages' explicitly confirm this. The notes state: 'Vertex ordering (CW/CCW) is not required for the containment test because it relies on dot product signs relative to the centroid.' The passages state: 'In this step, the sign of the dot product of the centroid with each normal vector defining each face will be stored (this prevents the need for knowing the CW / CCW ordering of the vertices)... If all the signs match, the point is internal to our (convex) element.' Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

A pixelization routine that transforms variable-resolution unstructured mesh values into an image buffer by depositing values through nearest-neighbor interpolation with anti-aliasing, decoupling the pixelization step from the underlying data model [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The passage explicitly states that the pixelization step transforms variable-resolution mesh values into an image buffer by depositing them through 'NN interpolation with anti-aliasing'. It also mentions that the routine accepts an interpolation kernel (nearest-neighbor) and decouples the pixelization step from the mesh values/data model by handling different mesh types and field definitions separately.

All specific details in the claim are present in the provided text.
